business_problem: Washington, DC agencies frequently need each other's data to deliver resident services, but legacy silos made sharing slow, copy-heavy, and governance-intensive. As sensors multiplied and data became more unstructured, that legacy platform became harder to maintain, harder to update, and harder for everyday users to work with.
solution_summary: Washington, DC agencies frequently need each other's data to deliver resident services, but legacy silos made sharing slow, copy-heavy, and governance-intensive. As the District’s centralized IT provider, the Office of the Chief Technology Officer (OCTO) sits at the intersection of more than 80 DC agencies — making secure, scalable data access essential. By deploying on the Databricks Data + AI Platform with Delta Sharing as an enterprise service, OCTO enabled secure, purpose-based cross-agency access without duplicating data, accelerating collaboration and cutting platform costs in half. Delivering services in Washington, DC rarely stops at one agency. A single resident request can touch multiple teams — from public safety and transportation to education, housing, and health and human services — and those agencies need to share data to act quickly.

solution_components.name: Databricks Data + AI Platform
solution_components.role: Provides the shared lakehouse environment for ingestion, engineering, analytics, and AI workloads.

solution_components.name: Delta Sharing
solution_components.role: Delivers governed data access across agencies, partners, or business units without copying datasets.

solution_components.name: Unity Catalog
solution_components.role: Applies centralized governance, lineage, and access controls across shared data assets.

data_flow: Operational, customer, and transactional data lands in Databricks, is transformed in the lakehouse under Unity Catalog governance, and is served to downstream users and applications through Delta Sharing.
business_outcome: Reported outcomes include 50% Lower data platform costs on Databricks; 10 Agencies onboarded in 1 year, surpassing 7 years on legacy system; 70k+ Residents’ wage outcomes analyzed across District education and workforce programs.
